It also must be presumed that when any law is made it is constitutionally valid until the presumption is rebutted by the person who challenges its validity. The United States Supreme Court in Middleton vs. Texas P & L Co 248 US 152, observed: 

 Bruen J in Gulf Colorado Rly vs. Ellis, 165 US 150, however, warned against carrying this presumption too far and observed: 

 "To carry the presumption to the extent of holding that there must be some undisclosed and unknown reason for subjecting certain individual or corporations to hostile and discriminatory legislation is to make the protection clause of the 14th Amendment a mere rope of sand." 

 76. A law cannot be struck down merely because it fails to spell out the particular objective of provision in the legislation itself. In the instant case the impugned clause (g) was brought in by the Local Government Laws (Amendment) Act 1997 (Act XXIII of 1987) apparently for the purpose of providing an additional ''''disqualification'''' for a person seeking election to an Union Parishad. For the purpose of withstanding a challenge to its constitutionality as being violative of Article 27 it was to stand the test of justification for being attached to Local Government body election only.And for that to begin with, item 7 of the propositions as above will be attracted ie the court ill presume the Constitutionality of a Statute until shown otherwise, Bhagwati, J in the case of R K Garg vs. Union of India AIR 1951 (SC) 2138 , reiterated that" the presumption of constitutionality is indeed so strong that in order to sustain it, the Court may take into consideration matters of common knowledge, matters of common report, the history of the times and may assume every state of facts which can be conceived existing at the time of legislation." 

 Relying on these decisions the learned Additional Attorney-General submits that it must be presumed that law is made consistent and valid unless the presumption is rebutted. He then submits that the Settlement Court was created for disposal of certain classes of cases relating to abandoned properties speedily and there is no violation of any rules or law and also there is no unreasonable classification amongst the owners within the area. 

 "14. The High Court Division, in our opinion, started with a wrong premise holding that the presumption of correctness of the entries in the Gazette Notification does not absolve the Government from denying the facts alleged by the claimant or from disclosing the  basis of treating ,the property as abandoned property when it is disputed. Section 5(2) of the Ordinance clearly provides that the list published under sub-section (1) shall be conclusive evidence of the fact that the buildings included therein are abandoned property and have vested in the Government, as such, section 7 says that a person claiming any right or interest in any such building may make an application to the Court of Settlement for exclusion of the building from such list, etc. on the ground that the building is not an abandoned building and has not vested in the Government under President's Order No. 16 of 1972 or that his right or interest in the building has not been affected by the provisions of that order. The onus, therefore, is squarely on the claimant of the building to prove that the building is not an abandoned property. The Government has no obligation either to deny the facts alleged by the claimant or to disclose the basis of treating the properly as abandoned property merely because the same is disputed by the claimant" 

 "Once a building is included in the list of abandoned properties it is conclusive, evidence that the building in question is an abandoned property where the owner either was not present in Bangladesh or his whereabouts were not known or he eased to manage or occupy the property at the time when President's Order 16 of 1972 was promulgated on 16-2-1972. This presumption is, of course, a rebuttable one. It is for the claimant to show that the original owner was present in Bangladesh or his whereabouts were known or he did not cease to occupy or manage the property in question at the relevant time. Since the notification in the official Gazette carries a presumption that the building in question is in abandoned property, it is exempt from any legal process be it an auction sale by the Government itself or through court" 

 "9. Admittedly, the property has been listed as an abandoned property. Thus the onus lies upon the petitioner to the but the presumption, provided in sub-section (2) of sections 5 that the same was not an abandoned property. No oral evidence has been adduced before the Settlement Court to prove that on 26-2-72 when President''''s Order 16 of 1972 was promulgated the original lessee, Naimuddin had been present in Bangladesh or his whereabouts were known or that he did not cease to occupy, supervise or manage in person the house in question. The Settlement Court upon assigning cogent reasons held that the kabala of the petitioner's vendor is a forged and fabricated document and the original lessee, Naimuddin did never appear physically before any authority for any purpose after the liberation war in Bangladesh. The High Court Division has thus, rightly, maintained the order of the Settlement Court by the impugned judgment and order. 

 11. In a number of cases we have already decided that enlistment of a building under section 5 of the Ordinance shall retain its position as an abandoned property, in view of the provision of sub-section (2) thereof, unless the presumption is rebutted that the same. is not an abandoned property within the meaning of Article 2 of President's Order No. 16 of 1972". 

 It is not denied that the petitioner purchased the disputed property and was in possession of the same since purchase on 14-10-64 and got his name mutated and paid rent up to 1986 in Miscellaneous Case No. 1019/76-77. He also filed the Nationality Certificate dated 30-4-77 issued by Pourashava Commissioner, Syedpur. An Affidavit sworn before a Magistrate on 27-4-86 has been filed to show petitioners allegiance to Bangladesh. He also submitted the voter list of the area to show that the name of the petition and other members of his family appear in the list as voters. All these facts and Government records clearly indicate that he is a citizen of Bangladesh. But it appears the learned Court of Settlement without considering this aspect rejected the petitioner on mere conjecture and surmises without any finding that the aforesaid records are forged. We find from the impugned judgment that the court held that'''' out of the petitioner's claim for 21 decimals of land he filed a kabala covering only 13½ decimals of land and he did not file any document for the remaining land claimed by him whereas both the documents were filed before the Court of Settlement but the Settlement Court did not take into consideration the other document covering the remaining land. The conclusiveness of proof of abandoned property as defined in section 5(2) of Ordinance 54/85 is rebuttable presumption as was held by their Lordships in the case of Bangladesh vs. Ashraf Ali reported in 49 DLR (AD) 161 relevant paragraph 8.
